dct_description_sm: Rapid warming in Northwest Territories is resulting in the thawing of permafrost creating hazards for new and existing infrastructure built on permafrost. Overall this project aimed to provide better informed decision information in the selection of sites for future development by providing maps that identify the current terrain compositions and conditions and rank the sites for future development. To do so, the project facilitated the application and further development of techniques and methods to monitor and predict the effects of permafrost subsidence and upheaval as a tool for climate change adaptation planning. Approaches and methodologies that had been successfully demonstrated in recent partner projects were augmented, in particular, the Remote Predictive Mapping techniques which utilize multi temporal RADAR and complimentary (in situ) data sources to measure surficial displacement.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: Permafrost Vertical Displacement Hazard Mapping using RADARSAT-2
